growerp.assessment.Assessment.description: Scores how well a revenue-first ERP rollout (website, marketing and sales before accounting, inventory and HR) fits a small company, and which phase to start with.

growerp.landing.LandingPage.title: Revenue-First ERP Assessment
growerp.landing.LandingPage.headline: Should your ERP start with sales instead of the back office?
growerp.landing.LandingPage.subheading: Answer 12 quick questions about your leads, sales and cash flow. You get a free, personalised report on whether a revenue-first rollout fits your business, and which phase to start with.

growerp.landing.PageSection.sectionTitle: Solve the Biggest Pain Point First
growerp.landing.PageSection.sectionDescription: Most companies under 30 employees share one problem: inconsistent leads, scattered customer data and disconnected sales tools. A revenue-first rollout deploys the ERP as the fix for that problem before it touches administration.

growerp.landing.PageSection.sectionTitle: A System That Pays for Itself
growerp.landing.PageSection.sectionDescription: Website, marketing and CRM come first, so the early phases generate revenue that funds the rest of the rollout. Cash flow is king, and a back-office-first project drains it without winning a single new customer.

growerp.landing.PageSection.sectionTitle: Add Complexity Only When Revenue Demands It
growerp.landing.PageSection.sectionDescription: Accounting arrives to measure the ROI of your sales, inventory and purchasing when order volume needs them, and HR only when manual processes genuinely break. Five phases, each with its own KPIs.

growerp.landing.CredibilityInfo.creatorBio: This assessment is built by the creators of GrowERP, a modern, open-source, multi-platform ERP built from modular building blocks.
growerp.landing.CredibilityInfo.backgroundText: Because GrowERP is modular, you can start with the website, marketing and CRM blocks and add accounting, inventory and HR later without a migration. This assessment uses that experience to tell you where to start.

growerp.landing.CredibilityStatistic.statistic: Faster time-to-value: the business sees financial benefit from the ERP in the first phase, not after a year of back-office setup.
Data-driven justification: the revenue KPIs captured in the early phases give hard numbers to justify every back-office module that follows.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: How many people work in your company?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: 1 to 9
More than 100

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: What is the biggest problem holding your business back right now?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: Not enough leads or new customers.
Leads and quotes slip through the cracks before they become orders.
Bookkeeping and invoicing take too much time.
Stock, purchasing or delivery can't keep up with orders.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: What does your website do for your sales today?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: We have no website, or only a brochure page.
Visitors can contact us, but enquiries land in an email inbox.
We capture leads or sell online, but in a separate tool.
Website leads and orders flow straight into our CRM and order system.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: Where does your customer and prospect information live?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: In people's heads, phones and email.
In spreadsheets.
Spread over several apps that don't talk to each other.
In one CRM that everybody uses.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: How does an interested customer become a paid order?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: Manual quotes in documents, then days or weeks of back and forth.
Quote templates, but orders and payments are re-typed elsewhere.
A sales tool creates quotes and orders, but payment is separate.
Approved quotes turn into orders and are paid online automatically.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: Do you know which marketing activity brought in last month's revenue?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: No idea.
A rough guess.
For some channels.
Yes, down to the campaign.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: How would you describe your cash flow?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: Tight: every new sale counts.
Stable, but we need growth to invest.
Well funded, with budget set aside for an ERP project.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: How are your back-office tasks (accounting, stock, HR) coping?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: Fine by hand or with our accountant.
Starting to strain, but manageable.
Regularly breaking under the order volume.
Our biggest problem: compliance, stock or payroll errors every month.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: How would the people who sell react to a new system?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: Eager, if it helps them close more deals.
The owner does the selling and wants less admin.
Hesitant; they are used to their own way of working.
Resistant; any change is a fight.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: How would you judge whether a new ERP was worth the money?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: More leads, more orders, more revenue.
Faster quotes and fewer lost deals.
Cleaner books and faster month-end.
Accurate stock and on-time deliveries.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: (Starting point) If you could fix one area in the next 90 days, which would it be?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: Website and marketing: attract visitors and capture leads.
CRM and orders: turn leads into quotes, orders and payments.
Accounting: invoice sales and see revenue per campaign.
Inventory and purchasing: deliver what we sell on time.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: (Solution) Which kind of help would suit you best?

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestionOpt.optionText: A free trial I can set up myself.
A guided setup of the website, marketing and CRM phases.
Full implementation support across all five phases.

growerp.assessment.AssessmentQuestion.questionText: (Open-Ended) Anything else we should know about your sales or marketing challenges?

growerp.assessment.ScoringThreshold.description: Strong revenue-first fit (70-100): your gap is turning visitors into leads and leads into paid orders. Start with Phase 1 (website, lead capture) and Phase 2 (CRM, quotes, online payment). Add the back office when revenue demands it.

Good revenue-first fit (40-69): some sales tools are in place but they are disconnected. Connect your website, CRM and orders first (Phases 1 and 2), then add accounting in Phase 3 to measure the revenue each campaign brings in.

Back-office first (0-39): your sales engine is already working and the strain is in fulfilment, accounting or HR. Start with Phase 3 or 4 (accounting, inventory and purchasing) and keep your current front-office tools connected.
